author: @Careermudhra_

content.text: One of the courses in the medical stream that has seen an increase in demand in recent years is BAMS or Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery, an undergraduate course offered by many reputed ayurveda colleges in India. The entire program is offered for 5.5 years, which includes a year of internship. Both government and private institutions offer undergraduate and postgraduate courses in Ayurveda and accept students through Ayush Counselling every year.

This article is about BAMS admission in India, which includes the eligibility criteria, fees, and how to get admission to top ayurvedic institutions in India. Let’s see an overview of the admission and seats offered for BAMS in India.

sections.heading: BAMS Admission 2025 Overview

content.text: Many reputed institutions and medical colleges provide BAMS admission in India. Admission to both private and government colleges follows the same guidelines, and the students are accepted through the Ayush NEET Counselling . AACCC and the concerned state counselling authorities are responsible for conducting the counselling process. Direct admission to BAMS without NEET is not possible, according to the Ministry of Ayush.

There is a total of 563 Ayurveda colleges for BAMS admission in India, according to the latest report of NCISM . The institutions offer Ayurveda courses adhering to the regulations of the Ministry of Ayush.
The following table shows the division of the number of colleges between govt/private/deemed/autonomous/aided/national institutes.

sections.heading: BAMS Eligibility Criteria

content.text: The candidates seeking BAMS admission should be aware of the eligibility requirements of the course to get into the reputed ayurveda colleges in the country.
NEET Qualification is mandatory for BAMS admission in India.

The NEET qualified candidates further need to participate in the Ayush counselling either for AIQ seats or State quota seats, according to the domicile of the candidates and preference of the college. The students should adhere to certain BAMS course eligibility criteria for BAMS admission in India. The criteria for admission are mentioned below.
Entrance Examination: NEET UG
Academic Qualification:

items: Pass in 10+2 from a recognized board and in the 12th with Physics, Chemistry, Biology/ Biochemistry as the core subjects.
Secure a minimum of 50% aggregate marks in the PCB subjects in the 12th standard. Candidates belonging to the reserved category are given 10% relaxation.

content.text: Age Limit: 17 or above in the year of admission.

sections.heading: BAMS Admission Process

content.text: BAMS admission in India includes NEET counselling. The procedure for BAMS admission in India is carried out by the AACCC and the state counselling authorities under the supervision of the Ministry of Ayush. The following are the step-by-step instructions for counselling and admission. Follow them thoroughly to avoid any inconvenience that may delay the admission process.
Step 1: Qualify NEET UG examination and register for Ayush Counselling in the AACCC portal for AIQ seats and the state counselling portal of the respective state for the state quota seats.
Step 2: Make payment of the counselling fees.
Step 3: Fill out the choices of colleges in the Choice filling/locking session.
Step 4: The Allotment List is published considering the NEET scores of the candidates, seats availability in the chosen colleges, and the reservation policy.
Step 5: Find your name in the Allotment List and report to the allotted college. If not allotted, you may participate in the further rounds of counselling.
Step 6: The students allotted shall provide their original documents and certificates to the college for document verification.
Step 7: Make payment of the fees to the college as instructed by them within the payment time limit to finalize admission and confirm your seat in the college.

There are generally 4 rounds of counselling, which involve registration and choice filling in each round. The candidates who are not allotted in any round may participate in the further rounds of counselling.

sections.heading: Documents Required for BAMS Admission in India

content.text: The students are required to carry with them certain documents and certificates in both original and photocopies for the document verification process at the college. Here’s the list of documents required for BAMS admission in India.

NEET Admit Card
NEET Score Card

Passport-size photos

Income Certificate (If applicable)
Disability Certificate (If applicable)

sections.heading: BAMS Course Fees in India

content.text: As per the norms of the Ministry of Ayush and the government of India, and the state governments, the Ayurveda colleges offer the BAMS program in different fee structures, depending on whether it is private or government institutions. Government colleges generally have a lower fee structure compared to private colleges. Private colleges charge extra expenses for the modern infrastructure and amenities they provide apart from the tuition fees. Make sure to go through the complete fee structure of the college you prefer before applying for BAMS admission in India.

sections.heading: Conclusion

content.text: BAMS is one of the AYUSH courses offered by colleges under the Ministry of Ayush. BAMS admission in India is accepted through the NEET UG examination and Ayush counselling. 563 Ayurveda colleges in India offer the BAMS program according to the NCISM. The candidates with 10+2 from a recognized board with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology are eligible for BAMS admission in India. sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
How to get admission in BAMS in India?

content.text: To get admission in BAMS in India, the candidates must qualify NEET and participate in the Ayush Counselling.

sections.heading: Can I join BAMS without NEET?

content.text: No, you cannot join BAMS without qualifying NEET exam.

sections.heading: What is the total fee of BAMS in India?

content.text: The total fee of BAMS in India for private colleges ranges from Rs 1.50 L to Rs 5 L annually, whereas for government colleges, it ranges from Rs 25K to Rs 75K for a year.

sections.heading: How many private BAMS Colleges are there in India?

content.text: There are 480 BAMS colleges in India.

sections.heading: What are the PG courses after BAMS?

content.text: After BAMS, you can join for PG courses such as, MD/MS (Ayurveda), which is offered in various specializations.

sections.heading: Can I apply for BAMS after 12th commerce?

content.text: No, you have to pass 12th with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology subjects to apply for BAMS.

sections.heading: How to apply for BAMS admission in India after qualifying NEET?

content.text: To apply for BAMS admission in India, after qualifying NEET, you must participate in the Ayush Counselling. You can give your choice of college in the choice filling round in the counselling.

sections.heading: How many seats are offered for BAMS admission in India?

content.text: 52,720 seats are offered for BAMS in India.
